patch_description:
This replaces the hardware-efficient ring circuit with a readout-aligned, Hamiltonian-inspired Floquet mixer. Every trainable gate shares one angle, leaving only one circuit parameter plus the fixed gain and bias. A collective RY layer changes the local measurement basis, while shared XX and reverse-ordered ZZ interactions act directly on the dataset-supplied readout graph. Because these generators do not generally commute on overlapping pairs, the three tied repetitions still produce a nonlinear correlated transformation rather than merely tripling one rotation.

The approach should generalize better in the few-shot regime because it uses the readout topology as an inductive bias, avoids qubit-specific parameters, and reduces optimization to a stable one-dimensional circuit search. It also improves parameter efficiency from five total parameters to three while retaining entangling capacity for difficult validation groups.
